title: Scaffold why-cast foundation
selection_reason: Empty repo required fast full-stack scaffolding, Cloudflare architecture decisions, and a simple frontend/API thin slice.
validations: Hackathon plan adapted from source execution plan
notes: Foundation ships a Cloudflare Worker MVP with curated Khan Academy source packs and browser speech synthesis as a temporary audio preview fallback.

title: Add Durable Object show rooms and judge-facing audio architecture
selection_reason: This bead touched Cloudflare runtime behavior, serialized continuity state, and live demo framing, so one integrated platform pass was the fastest safe path.
validations: Durable Object binding and migration added
notes: Serialized shows now live in Durable Objects, and the API/UI explicitly frame the Cloudflare plus multi-API ElevenLabs architecture for judges.

title: Add prompt-driven workflow demo artifacts
selection_reason: This bead built the full demo narrative layer needed by the landing page and hackathon walkthrough: prompt bundle, draft, editor pass, continuity memory, and workflow stages.
validations: Editor and continuity artifacts returned in production
notes: The live API now exposes a full workflow-demo payload suitable for landing-page storytelling and hackathon judging, while preserving a future swap to real LLM generation.

title: Add family quiz gate and workflow orchestration
selection_reason: This bead connected Durable Objects, Workflows, quiz-based feedback loops, and reminder planning into one coherent Cloudflare-native flow for the hackathon demo.
validations: Serialized show creation returned workflow runtime IDs
Quiz-submit route unlocked Episode 2 in production
Reminder planning artifacts returned in API
notes: why-cast now uses Cloudflare Workflows for pipeline and reminder orchestration, plus a small family quiz to unlock the next serialized episode and reduce spammy auto-generation.

title: Add narrator presets and live generation route
selection_reason: This bead combined the last high-value MVP pieces: narrator selection, on-site sampling, deployed OpenAI-backed live generation, and the supporting docs needed for a believable demo.
validations: Narrator presets returned in production config
Live generated script returned without template section labels
notes: The app now supports four selectable narrator presets and a real OpenAI-backed Episode 1 generation path, while server-side ElevenLabs narration remains pending only because the deployed Worker does not yet have an ElevenLabs API key.

title: Add ElevenLabs audio rendering and playback
selection_reason: This bead touched the audio path across the Worker, Durable Object storage, narrator presets, and the site UI, so one integrated platform pass was the fastest safe way to finish the MVP slice.
validations: GET /api/config returned elevenLabsReady true in production
GET /api/narrators/:narratorPresetId/sample returned real audio in production
POST /api/shows/:showId/render-audio stored Episode 1 audio in the Durable Object
GET /api/shows/:showId/episodes/:episodeId/audio streamed stored audio back in production
notes: why-cast now supports real server-rendered narrator samples and Episode 1 audio playback/download using ElevenLabs plus Durable Object-backed storage, with R2 still next for longer-lived audio hosting.

title: Ship React landing page and preserve live demo flow
selection_reason: This bead spanned frontend architecture, Worker asset delivery, and the production demo flow, so a single product-platform pass was the fastest way to improve visual quality without breaking the working backend.
validations: GET / returned the new React landing page in production
GET /api/config still returned narrator presets and elevenLabsReady true
POST /api/shows succeeded from the deployed app shell
POST /api/shows/:showId/generate-live succeeded after the frontend migration
POST /api/shows/:showId/render-audio and GET /api/shows/:showId/episodes/:episodeId/audio both succeeded after the live-script trimming safeguard
notes: The landing page now uses a React + Vite frontend served by the same Worker, and the full create -> generate-live -> render-audio path remains working in production after trimming oversized live scripts for the temporary Durable Object audio-storage path.
